title: audit-logging: add audit-event registry + build-time check for unregistered event names
author: Sahana Iyer
description: Context: As part of the audit logging program (schema v1 + coverage enforcement), we need to prevent services from emitting arbitrary event_name values that aren’t registered/validated. This PR introduces a centralized audit-event registry in-repo plus a build-time check that fails CI when new event names are used without being added to the registry. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a canonical registry file for audit event names with ownership + schema version metadata, (2) Adds a small build tool that scans for audit event emissions and validates they reference registry entries, (3) Wires the check into the monorepo build (runs on CI + pre-submit), (4) Updates developer docs with “how to add a new audit event” guidance and naming constraints. Notes/constraints: This is not runtime enforcement; runtime validation still happens in the audit pipeline + shared library. The build check is intended to catch mistakes early and standardize naming. The scanner is conservative by default (only flags patterns we control, e.g., Audit.Log(eventName=...) and auditlog.Emit("...") wrappers) to avoid false positives. Follow-ups: expand scanner coverage for a few legacy call sites and migrate remaining direct string usage to typed constants (tracked in ENG-2482).
commits: build: add audit-event registry checker (go tool)
ci: wire audit-event-registry check into presubmit pipeline
docs: add audit event registration workflow + examples
refactor: migrate gateway + console backend to use typed event constants
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we clarify in the docs that the registry is the source of truth for event_name values (and that services should not invent new strings)? Also, please align examples with the naming guideline namespaces (api.*, console.*, rbac.*) discussed in architecture. Sahana Iyer (author): Updated docs/security/audit-logging.md to explicitly state registry is authoritative and added a short section on namespaces; also updated examples to api.api_key.* and rbac.role.*. Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Scanner approach looks good. One concern: regex-based scanning tends to miss a lot of cases. Can we ensure we only enforce for the shared library wrappers so we don’t block teams with false positives? Sahana Iyer (author): Yes—scanner only matches our wrappers and typed constants packages. Added tests demonstrating it won’t flag arbitrary strings outside auditlog.Emit(...) / Audit.Log(...). Nadia Rahman (review): Where does ownership live? For coverage enforcement we’ll want to know which team owns adding events + ensuring fields are populated. Suggest adding owner and subsystem in registry entries. Sahana Iyer (author): Added required fields `owner_team` and `subsystem` to registry.yaml and validation in registry parser; updated a handful of initial entries. Marcus Lin (review): Please make sure the tool fails closed only for new/modified packages, otherwise we’ll be stuck fixing legacy call sites before landing. Also, we should treat this as a security control—ensure the failure is hard (non-optional) on main CI. Sahana Iyer (author): Implemented “changed-packages mode” using git diff against base SHA in CI; still hard-fails for any changed package introducing unregistered event names. Wired it into the required Buildkite step on main. Benji Okafor (review): Nit: registry.yaml should include schema version and an optional legacy_aliases field for the dual-write migration work. Sahana Iyer (author): Added `schema_version: v1` and `legacy_aliases` (optional) to entry schema; docs include when to populate (only during migration windows). Final approvals: Allison Grant (approved), Nadia Rahman (approved), Kaitlyn Nguyen (approved), Marcus Lin (approved).
release_notes: Internal: added centralized audit-event registry and CI gate to prevent emitting unregistered audit event names; updated developer docs for adding new audit events.
